THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 10.06.2021 IN MVC NO.251/2016 PASSED BY THE COURT OF II ADDL.

DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE BIDAR SITTING AT BASAVAKALYAN, AND CONSEQUENTLY ALLOW THE PRESENT APPEAL THEREBY ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION RS.54,42,000/- AS CLAIMED IN THE PRESENT APPEAL, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, B.M.SHYAM PRASAD., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These appeals are filed calling in question the judgment and award dated 10.06.2021 insofar as the claim petition in MVC No.251/2016 on the file of the II Addl. District and Sessions Judge & MACT,
Bidar sitting at Basavakalyan [for short, 'the Tribunal'].
2.

sentences.text: The appeal in MFA No.201445/2022 is by the Insurer of the offending motor car bearing Reg.No.MH-24- AX-6217, and the appeal in MFA No.200046/2022 is by the claimants.
The Tribunal by this common judgment dated NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB 10.06.2021 has also decided another claim petition in MVC No.252/2016.

It is stated that the Insurer has filed a separate appeal calling in question this judgment insofar as the other claim petition in MVC No.252/2016, and this appeal is pending before the learned Single Judge of this Court.
The claimants and the Insurer are referred to accordingly for reasons of convenience.

3. Sri Sanjay M. Joshi, the learned counsel for the Insurer, and Sri Ameet Kumar Deshpande, the learned Senior Counsel for the claimants, are heard for final disposal upon perusal of the records including the trial Court records.
It is obvious from the submissions that there is no dispute that Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole, the claimants' son, has died in a road accident on 02.05.2015.

The deceased Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole was traveling in a car bearing Reg.No.MH-24-AX-6217,
which was being driven by one Sri Syed Sarfaraz.
The offending vehicle i.e., tanker bearing Reg.No.MH-13-AX-4689, coming from the opposite side, dashed against the car in which Sri Roopesh Kumar NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB Tambole was travelling.

Apart from Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole, his wife and their minor son have also breathed their last in the said accident and only one of the minor sons, who is a claimant in MVC No.252/2016, has survived.

4. The Tribunal's finding that the accident is because of the driver of the tanker remains undisputed,
it also remains undisputed that the tanker was insured with the Insurer as of the date of the accident.
Nevertheless, the Insurer has disputed its liability, and in this appeal proposes to challenge the quantum of compensation awarded.

The Tribunal has awarded a total sum of Rs.1,24,58,000/-
as compensation to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

The computation of this compensation is under the following heads:
Loss of dependency Rs.1,24,08,368/-
 Other heads Rs.50,000/-

Sri Sanjay M. Joshi submits that the tanker is insured based on the details of the vehicle furnished by the owner of the tanker, who had obtained insurance policy furnishing certain chassis number and engine number, but as could be seen from the police records though the registration number remains the same, the engine and chassis number have been changed.

The offending vehicle is insured based on certain parameters but if the constitution of the very vehicle which is made up by its chassis and engine is changed, then the Insurer, and the Tribunal has failed to consider this crucial fact.

6. On the question of quantum, Sri Sanjay M. Joshi submits that the Insurer would not dispute the addition to be made towards future prospects or application of multiplier based on the age of Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole or deduction to be made at 50% because the claimants are the parents of Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole and he is their only son.

However, the Insurer disputes the amount awarded towards loss of dependency because the Tribunal, NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB instead of taking the average of three years income as per the income tax returns, has taken the sum total of three years income and has computed the loss of dependency.

7. Sri Ameet Kumar Deshpande submits that the Insurer has not taken up defence of the change in the engine and chassis numbers in the statement of objections and this defence is evolved when the details of the registration certificate and driving license are produced as exhibits by the claimants.
The owner of the tanker was by then placed ex parte, and in any event Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole, who was traveling as an inmate would be a third party.

The Insurer, to answer its liability in law to pay just and reasonable compensation, must pay the claimants, and if it could vindicate its defence, it must recover the amount from the owner of the tanker.

8. On the question of computation towards loss of dependency on the grounds urged by Sri Sanjay M. Joshi, Sri Ameet Kumar Deshpande canvasses that this Court must take the average of three years income as brought out NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB not just by the returns filed prior to the date of accident but also thereafter.

The returns though filed after the date of the accident, relates to the income that the Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole had earned prior to the date of accident and hence, the returns filed after the date of the accident cannot be discarded as irrelevant or as having no The Manager vs Shashikala W/O Jagannath Tambole And ... on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44611305/
5 evidentiary value.
He also canvasses that this Court must deduct just the tax paid but not any interest that is levied for delay in filing the returns of paying taxes and that in the circumstances of this case where Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole is shown to have been engaged in a profitable business at a very young age, there must be a higher rate of interest than 6% awarded by the Tribunal.
9.

sentences.text: In the light of the undisputed fact that Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole was travelling as an inmate insofar as the Insurer, he would be a third party.
Even if the Insurer could vindicate its defence, it cannot avoid liability to pay just and reasonable compensation to the claimants.
The Insurer, at the most, may recover the amount paid from - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB the owner of the tanker.

The question whether the Insurer must recover from the owner of the insured vehicle is a question that must generally be decided in a proceedings filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 but in cases where the owner has remained absent and the Courts could opine, given the nature of the breach alleged and the stay at which the particular defences are taken and the evidence placed on record, or any other circumstances that could be material, it should be open in law to defer the question of recovery from the owner in the proceedings that the Insurer must initiate against the concerned to recover after paying the third party.

10. In the present case, on perusal of the statement of objections and the other records, this Court must opine that there is considerable force in the submissions of Sri Ameet Kumar Deshpande that the defence to deny the liability alleging that chassis and the engine numbers have been altered, is evolved during the trial without necessary pleadings in the statement of objections.
The owner of the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB tanker has not participated in the enquiry.

This Court is therefore of the view that the Insurer must be called upon to answer the claim of the present claimants with liberty to initiate proceedings, as is permissible in law to recover from the owner with liberty to such owner to contest the Insurer's case.
The first question must necessarily be answered in these terms.
11. The deceased's income tax assessment for the year 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15 with the necessary auditor's report have been marked as Exs.P-31 to 33, respectively.

The returns filed for the assessment year 2013-14 is subject to assessment order under Section 143 of the Income Tax Act,
1961.
Initially, a sum of Rs.3,32,525/- was filed as income but with the assessment scrutiny, the income is taken at Rs.5,93,850/-.

The income for the three years assessment therefore would be Rs.5,44,039/-, Rs.5,93,850/- and Rs.4,82,212/- and Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole for the corresponding years has paid taxes in sums of Rs.42,032/-, Rs.50,233/- and Rs.27,008/-.

6 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole has also paid statutory interest for delay in paying the aforesaid taxes but that cannot be deducted out of the income.
12. Sri Ameet Kumar Deshpande has argued that the income of the deceased as per the return filed for the assessment year 2015-16 must be considered.
But it remains undisputed that this return is not audited.

It would be difficult to uphold the probative value of this return in favour of the claimants in view of the fact that though a higher return are filed for this assessment year it is not audited while the returns filed for the previous assessment years are audited with necessary audit reports being annexed.
Therefore, unaudited returns cannot be considered to arrive at a just and reasonable compensation.
The average income of the earlier three years as per the return filed, after deducting the income tax paid, must be considered.
The average income when so considered would be in a sum of Rs.5,00,276/-.

As Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole was aged 28 years as of the date of accident, the appropriate addition towards future prospects would be 40% of his income and the multiplier, which is undisputed, would be 17.
The deduction towards personal expenses will be 50%.

With these changes the loss of dependency would be in a sum of Rs.59,53,284.4/- computed thus:
 Description By this Court  Annual Income Rs.5,00,276.00  Addition of 40% towards  future prospects to the Rs.7,00,386.4  annual income  Deduction of 50% towards  Rs.3,50,193.2  personal expenses  Loss of Dependency Rs.59,53,284.4/-
14.
In addition, the claimants, who are parents of Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole, would be entitled to consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each and conventional sum of Rs.30,000/-.
Thus the claimants would be entitled for a total sum of Rs.60,63,300/- as compensation.

For the foregoing, the following:
 ORDER  [i] The appeals stand disposed of modifying the Tribunal's judgment and award dated 10.06.2021 insofar MVC No.251/2016.

[ii] The Insurer shall pay a sum of Rs.63,94,700/- to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of eight weeks [8] from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB [iii] The Insurer, upon payment of the compensation as aforesaid, shall be entitled to recover such amount and every other amount that would be permissible under law from the owner of the insured vehicle.
However, the owner of the vehicle is reserved liberty to contest the Insurer's entitlement to recover from him.
It is observed that all questions on this aspect are left open to be decided in such proceedings.

The average income when so considered would be in a sum of Rs.5,00,276/-.
As Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole was aged 28 years as of the date of accident, the appropriate addition towards future prospects would be 40% of his income and the multiplier, which is undisputed, would be 17.
The deduction towards personal expenses will be 50%.
With these changes the loss of dependency would be in a sum of Rs.59,53,284.4/- computed thus:
 Description By this Court  Annual Income Rs.5,00,276.00  Addition of 40% towards  future prospects to the Rs.7,00,386.4  annual income  Deduction of 50% towards  Rs.3,50,193.2  personal expenses  Loss of Dependency Rs.59,53,284.4/-
14.
In addition, the claimants, who are parents of Sri Roopesh Kumar Tambole, would be entitled to consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each and conventional sum of Rs.30,000/-.
Thus the claimants would be entitled for a total sum of Rs.60,63,300/- as compensation.

For the foregoing, the following:
 ORDER  [i] The appeals stand disposed of modifying the Tribunal's judgment and award dated 10.06.2021 insofar MVC No.251/2016.
[ii] The Insurer shall pay a sum of Rs.63,94,700/- to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of eight weeks [8] from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1411-DB [iii] The Insurer, upon payment of the compensation as aforesaid, shall be entitled to recover such amount and every other amount that would be permissible under law from the owner of the insured vehicle.
However, the owner of the vehicle is reserved liberty to contest the Insurer's entitlement to recover from him.
It is observed that all questions on this aspect are left open to be decided in such proceedings.
